items.claim: Both boundaries rest on tier-1 signals rather than the tier-3 mark alone, and the row discloses a genuine, non-strawman rival instead of suppressing it.
items.evidence: Byte collation confirms the eschatological formula opens Isa.2.2 as a fresh promise distinct from the ha-davar header it follows, and the row correctly names the true closing driver as the imperative-vocative that opens Isa.2.5 rather than resting the close on the petuchah break alone; the shared "house of Jacob" catchword between Isa.2.3 and Isa.2.5 is honestly disclosed as live tension rather than hidden.

items.claim: The opening addressee shift is a genuine tier-1 signal and the closing refrain is byte-confirmed identical to its Isa.2.17 counterpart, with the single-oracle rival honestly disclosed rather than strawmanned.
items.evidence: Byte collation of the refrain shows the closing clause "וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא" at Isa.2.11 is identical letter-for-letter to "וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא" at Isa.2.17, while the preceding pride/loftiness clause varies in word order between the two sites exactly as the row discloses at the correct tier; the row's own rejected alternative (one unbroken Isa.2.5-22 oracle) is the real live rival, not a strawman.

items.claim: The row treats Isa.2.12 as a fresh unit onset without disclosing that it is grammatically continuative and lexically bonded to the refrain it treats as the prior unit's clean close.
items.evidence: Isa.2.12 opens with the particle "כִּ֣י", which elsewhere in this same span (Isa.2.6, inside the preceding unit's own address) functions to continue rather than launch a fresh address; and its own diction -- "עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם" and "וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל" -- directly recycles the pride/humbling vocabulary of the refrain that just closed the preceding row at Isa.2.11 ("שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים"), which itself echoes Isa.2.9's "וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל אִ֑ישׁ", and continues on into the catalogue's repeated lofty/lifted-up forms at Isa.2.13-14. This byte-true device straddling the row's own opening seam is left undisclosed, weakening (without necessarily defeating) the claimed fresh-onset warrant and leaving the strongest rival -- a single sustained poem on pride and humbling running from at least Isa.2.9 through the refrain-punctuated catalogue, with the refrain functioning as internal punctuation rather than a hard division -- unstated.

items.claim: The topical-shift boundary is grounded in the prior row's own tier-1 refrain closure, the third-stanza rival is honestly rejected rather than ignored, and the recurring temporal tag is accurately disclosed as continuing texture rather than a reopened refrain.
items.evidence: Byte collation confirms Isa.2.20 opens with the same in-that-day temporal formula the row cites, and Isa.2.22 carries no recurrence of the closing refrain clause, supporting the row's own claim that the unit is bounded by topic and the closing petuchah rather than a forced third refrain-bracketed stanza.

items.claim: The hinneh-announcement open and the byte-confirmed causal continuation at Isa.3.8 justify keeping Isa.3.1-12 as one unit, and the row correctly withholds a woe_oracle tag despite two internal occurrences of a different, easily-confused interjection.
items.evidence: Byte collation confirms Isa.3.8 opens with a causal particle explaining the collapse announced at Isa.3.1, supporting the row's rejection of a 3:1-7/3:8-12 split; and Isa.3.9 and Isa.3.11 both carry the short 'oy' interjection rather than the book's 'hoy' woe-onset lexeme, matching the row's disclosed distinction and correctly keeping the unit tagged judgment_oracle rather than woe_oracle.

items.claim: The row's disclosed rival addresses a unit_type labeling choice rather than a genuine competing boundary, leaving its actual strongest segmentation rival unstated.
items.evidence: The row's strongest_rejected_alternative argues trial_speech over judgment_oracle as a classification matter, which is already covered separately in device_notes as the mandated deviation disclosure; it never tests a real competing span for this row's own boundaries -- e.g. whether the riv/din speech should instead continue merged into the following material at the next narrative onset, or remain undivided from the leadership-collapse unit immediately preceding it. The field is repurposed for a classification argument instead of a segmentation rival, so the row's actual strongest rejected alternative is never disclosed.

items.claim: The row's own grammatical label for the Isa.3.18-23 catalogue is imprecise, though its underlying single-unit conclusion is sound.
items.evidence: Isa.3.18 opens with a single finite verb, "יָסִ֣יר" (he will take away), governing an accumulating list of accusative objects across Isa.3.18-23, not a construct/genitive chain as the row's own prose labels it; the mischaracterized grammatical term doesn't affect the row's correct conclusion that the catalogue is enumeration inside one governed clause rather than an independent list-register unit.

items.claim: The row's remnant-family signal tag blends two lexically distinct roots at Isa.4.3 as if they were one family.
items.evidence: "הַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר" at Isa.4.3 is the verb form of the book's remnant root, but "וְהַנּוֹתָר֙" in the same verse is a different root -- the one behind "וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה" describing the besieged daughter of Zion at Isa.1.8, which the row's own device_notes elsewhere treats as a merely skeleton-tier, differently-rooted match to Isa.4.6's pavilion noun. That same care is not extended at Isa.4.3: the second, differently-rooted synonym is tagged under the remnant-family signal alongside the true remnant-root form without disclosing they are two roots paired in synonymous parallelism, a blended sweep the book's own count-discipline forbids.
